svg.title: Circulation & health
svg.desc: Double circulation: The left ventricle has a thicker muscular wall for higher pressure. Valves stop backflow. Coronary arteries supply heart muscle. Heart rate & flow: Pacemaker cells in the right atrium set the rhythm. Artificial pacemakers correct irregularities. Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume 70 beats/min × 75 cm³/beat = 5,250 cm³/min = 5.25 dm³/min. Vessels & lungs: Arteries: thick muscle and elastic walls withstand high pressure. Veins: wide lumen and valves help return blood. Capillaries: one-cell-thick walls give a short exchange path. Alveoli: large area, thin walls, blood flow and ventilation. Oxygen moves to blood. Carbon dioxide moves to air. Blood components: Red cells: haemoglobin binds oxygen. Biconcave shape gives a large area. No nucleus leaves space for haemoglobin. White cells: phagocytosis, antibodies and antitoxins. Platelets: clotting. Plasma: transports cells, nutrients, hormones, carbon dioxide and urea. Distributes heat. Disease & treatment: Fatty deposits narrow coronary arteries, reducing oxygen for heart-muscle respiration. Stents: keep arteries open. Statins: lower cholesterol. Faulty valves leak or restrict flow. Biological or mechanical replacements restore flow. Compare donor or artificial hearts: benefit, surgery, blood-clot risk and possible rejection of donor tissue. Health & cancer: Health: physical and mental well-being. Diseases can interact. Lifestyle, environment and genes affect risk. Smoking damages lungs and raises cancer risk. Obesity raises Type 2 diabetes risk. Alcohol can damage the liver and brain. Cancer: uncontrolled division. Benign: local. Malignant: invades and forms secondary tumours. Correlation alone is not causation. Compare representative rates and social/financial costs.
